- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) and price drops, model frequently undercorrects; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to counteract mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices when sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00–0.33) and recent price action is trending down; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5%.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term mean reversion; if 10-day average is >10% above recent 5-day high, reduce forecast by 1–2%.
- When sentiment is bullish but price is falling, model tends to ignore sentiment; if sentiment >0.67 and price < prior 5-day low, add 0.5–1.0% upward adjustment.
